scenario: A music streaming analytics report covers only songs that reached more than 1 million streams, as the platform considers these 'charted'. A record label A&R executive uses the average stream count among charted songs to set targets for new artists.

data.description: Report only covers songs with > 1M streams. Underlying stream count distribution across all released songs assumed Normal with known standard deviation Ïƒ = 0.8M streams.

question: Charted songs average 1.5M streams. Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean stream count Î¼ across ALL released songs (including those that never charted), and (b) the fraction of all songs that reach the charting threshold.
naive_answer: A typical song gets about 1.5M streams since that is the charted-song average.
naive_trap: About 71% of songs never reach 1M streams and are excluded from the report. The true mean across all releases is just 0.55M. Setting artist targets based on charted-song averages would create systematically unrealistic expectations for the vast majority of releases.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(1.0-mu)/0.8; sf=norm.sf(a); return mu+0.8*norm.pdf(a)/sf-1.5 if sf>1e-10 else 1e10
mu=brentq(eq,0.3,0.7)
assert abs(mu-0.5512)<0.025
assert abs(norm.sf((1.0-mu)/0.8)-0.2874)<0.01
